name: Anarcho-Capitalism
description: Private property and market exchange without a state.

name: Anarcho-Communism
description: Communal ownership and anti-authoritarian federation.

name: Anarcho-Syndicalism
description: Worker organization and direct industrial action under anarchist commitments.

name: Individualist Anarchism
description: Anti-authoritarian self-direction and voluntary association without a single required economic program.

name: Market Anarchism
description: An anarchist family anchor for voluntary exchange and non-state coordination, without deciding among capitalist, mutualist, or counter-economic variants.

name: Minarchism
description: A minimal state limited to protective and adjudicative functions.

name: Mutualism (family-level)
description: A family-level affinity for reciprocal exchange, federated association, and opposition to privilege; it does not identify Proudhonian, Tuckerite, Labadie-line, Swartz-associated, or later mutualist and left-market variants—or affiliation with C4SS or any writer.

name: Social / Communal Anarchism
description: A family-level experimental affinity for anti-authoritarian, communal, and federated social organization. It does not make mutualism, market anarchism, syndicalism, anarcho-communism, or a single transition strategy a required subtype.

name: Conservative / Prudential Conservative
description: Broad prudential continuity and gradual institutional change.

name: Liberal Conservatism / Conservative Liberalism
description: Constitutional liberty and markets combined with social and institutional continuity.

name: National Conservatism
description: National continuity joined to conservative institutional politics.

name: Neoconservatism
description: Modern U.S. conservative internationalism with an assertive foreign-policy orientation.

name: Social Conservatism
description: Moral and family traditionalism as a cross-cutting political commitment.

name: Anarcha-Feminism
description: Treats patriarchy as intertwined with state and other hierarchical domination and favors decentralized, anti-authoritarian forms of liberation and organization.

name: Liberal Feminism
description: Centers individual autonomy, equal citizenship, equal opportunity, and legal-institutional reform within a liberal-democratic framework.

name: Radical Feminism
description: Treats patriarchy and male dominance as a distinct structural system, with sexuality, reproduction, and family relations central sites of political power.

name: Socialist / Marxist Feminism
description: Explains gender domination through the interaction of patriarchy with class, property, paid labor, unpaid care work, and social reproduction.

name: Deep Ecology
description: Strong independent moral standing for nonhuman nature.

name: Degrowth Green
description: Democratic reduction of material throughput in affluent economies.

name: Ecomodernism
description: Ecological improvement through innovation, infrastructure, and high-capacity institutions.

name: Ecosocialism
description: Ecological transformation joined to collective ownership and anti-capitalist politics.

name: Green Capitalism
description: Market investment and regulation as the main route to ecological transition.

name: Black community-autonomy orientation
description: Emphasizes Black community autonomy, institution-building, self-reliance, and collective power without requiring territorial separation or independent statehood.

name: Black separatist self-determination orientation
description: Combines Black collective autonomy with a stronger preference for territorial separation, independent political authority, or separate statehood.

name: Ethnonationalism
description: Defines nationhood primarily through inherited descent and culture and gives political weight to congruence between the state and the historic core nation.

name: Indigenous sovereignty and resurgence
description: Centers Indigenous collective self-government, treaty and territorial authority, and negotiated restoration of political jurisdiction within or alongside existing states.

name: Indigenous sovereignty and resurgence
description: Treats settler-colonial authority and dispossession as continuing structures and emphasizes resurgence, refusal, land-based political relations, and rebuilding Indigenous institutions on their own terms.

name: Multiculturalism
description: Supports recognition and accommodation of cultural difference within shared citizenship, including differentiated rights or self-government where justified.

name: Pan-African solidarity and unity
description: Treats African peoples and African-descended diasporas as linked by political interests that can justify transnational solidarity, coordination, or African political unity across existing state borders.

name: Absolute Monarchism
description: Hereditary authority with concentrated sovereign power.

name: Constitutional Monarchism
description: Monarchy constrained by constitutional and elected institutions.

name: Democratic Confederalism
description: Decentralized, pluralist, and confederal democratic organization.

name: Libertarian Municipalism
description: Municipal democracy and confederal self-government.

name: Traditional Monarchism
description: Hereditary authority grounded in historical and social continuity.

name: Hindutva
description: A majoritarian or civilizational account of Indian national identity centered on Hindu cultural belonging.

name: Islamic Democratic Constitutionalism
description: Popular sovereignty and constitutional competition interpreted through Islamic legal and ethical traditions.

name: Political Islam
description: Political projects that make Islamic identity or law central to state and movement politics.

name: Religious Nationalism
description: An umbrella fusion of religious identity and national goals whose institutional forms vary over law, citizenship, authority, and minority rights.

name: Theocratic Politics (religious-legal authority)
description: A family-level experimental affinity for final religious authority over civil-law legitimacy. It does not identify a religion, clerical office, constitutional form, or treatment of minorities.

name: Zionism
description: A family of Jewish national self-determination projects with divergent territorial and constitutional variants.

name: Council Communism
description: Worker councils and direct democratic control of production and politics.

name: Democratic Socialism
description: Democratic control or social ownership pursued through pluralist and accountable institutions, with variation over reform and transition.

name: Guild Socialism
description: Democratic worker control and public or social ownership organized through self-governing functional associations.

name: Maoism
description: Revolutionary party organization, mass mobilization, and centralized transition.

name: Market Socialism
description: Social ownership combined with market exchange or competition.

name: Marxian Socialism
description: A non-Leninist Marxian family centered on class analysis and social ownership, without requiring a party-state model.

name: Social Democracy
description: Reformist welfare and labor politics within a mixed economy.

name: Syndicalism
description: Union organization and direct industrial action as the route to social transformation.

name: Trotskyism
description: Revolutionary Marxism emphasizing international transformation and party strategy.

name: Accelerationism
description: Strategic intensification of technological or social change to transform existing institutions.

name: Cyberocracy
description: Governance through cybernetic information systems and algorithmic administration.

name: Dataism
description: An epistemic and cultural orientation that gives data-driven systems privileged interpretive authority.

name: Left Accelerationism
description: A post-capitalist accelerationist current that seeks to redirect technological and economic capacities beyond capitalist social relations.

name: Right Accelerationism
description: A market-intensifying accelerationist current associated with deepening competition, technological disruption, and the weakening of existing political arrangements.

name: Techno-Anarchism
description: Decentralized technology and cryptography used against centralized control.

name: Technocratic Centralism
description: Centralized expert administration insulated from ordinary electoral pressure.

name: Technology-Centered Accelerationism
description: A technology-first accelerationist current whose political-economic destination is less specified than its commitment to intensification.
